Pfizer, fresh to China’s obesity market, looks to Viagra model to compete
snippet: Pfizer is calling upon lessons learned from one of the first drugs ever made available on the internet—Viagra—as it commercializes a new obesity drug in China.

title: Compass to submit psilocybin depression drug for approval imminently after stock wobbles
snippet: Compass Pathways revealed that an FDA filing for COMP360 will be complete “in the next two weeks,” with an expected drug launch in the first half of next year. The update follows a reported regulatory submission for Usona Institute’s own psilocybin candidate for depression on Monday.

title: Lonza agrees to buy 5 Merck KGaA facilities to accelerate US expansion
snippet: The Swiss contract development and manufacturing organization will more than double its U.S. footprint by acquiring the Merck KGaA plants.

title: Neurocrine defends Prader-Willi drug after another patient death
snippet: Neurocrine Biosciences will conduct a new study for the rare disease drug Vykat to explore dosing and safety in patients with Prader-Willi syndrome who have complex health issues.

title: Novartis puts $772M BioArctic deal on ice, skates away from brain-delivery alliance
snippet: Novartis is discontinuing a neurodegeneration alliance with BioArctic in which the companies aimed to develop a drug candidate that could cross the blood-brain barrier.

title: Pfizer flat in Q3 despite 32% growth for new and acquired products
snippet: Sales of assets from Seagen and Biohaven grew in the third quarter, but it wasn’t enough for Pfizer to overcome declines across the Prevnar and COVID franchises.

title: Karyopharm files for bankruptcy, looks to merger with Ayrmid for life raft
snippet: Debtor-in-process financing up to $55 million could keep the lights on at Karyopharm Therapeutics for its multiple myeloma and myelofibrosis programs as the biotech waits to see if its union with Ayrmid will go through.

title: FDA peptide policy risks undermining drug development and patient safety
snippet: By allowing compounding pharmacies to produce certain unapproved peptides, the Department of Health and Human Services could, in the short term, put patients in harm’s way. Longer term, the policy shift threatens the industry that brings new medicines to market.

title: Sun Pharma stops eye-care drug production at Indian plant amid quality issues
snippet: The cessation of manufacturing activities follows a Sun Pharma recall and reports that regulators found fault with the company’s quality system.

title: Tiziana touts multiple sclerosis win at lower dose as high dose misses mark
snippet: In a mid-stage trial, the lower dose of Tiziana’s intranasal monoclonal antibody reduced microglial activation in a specific type of multiple sclerosis. But the path forward remains unclear after the higher dose failed to deliver the same benefit.

title: Vistagen cuts workforce for second time in 2026
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Cell therapy investment grows as safety events rankle Big Pharma's CAR T autoimmune push
snippet: Sail Biomedicine’s $925 million deal with Johnson & Johnson helped boost the cell and gene therapy sector over biologics in terms of venture capital fundraising in the third quarter.

title: U.S. bioscience jobs up 7% from 2021 to 2025: Report
snippet: Bioscience employment rose in 41 states, though not in California, according to a new report from the Biotechnology Innovation Organization and the Council of State Bioscience Associations.

title: UniQure snags May Day decision date for Huntington’s gene therapy after arduous year
snippet: After a year of controversial regulatory reversals, the FDA has accepted uniQure’s application for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec for priority review, with a May 1 action date. If approved, the therapy—also called AMT-130—would be the first disease-modifying treatment for Huntington’s disease.

title: Significant stock movers of October: Biohaven climbs, ArriVent dives
snippet: A fresh FDA review for Biohaven’s embattled ataxia drug lifted the biotech's shares, while a late-stage lung cancer miss battered ArriVent, which failed to rebound even after encouraging early ADC data.

title: Drugmakers rush to pair up with Summit’s ivonescimab ahead of key verdict
snippet: With companies including AstraZeneca, Pfizer and Revolution Medicines clamoring to get in on Summit Therapeutics’ Akeso-partnered PD-1xVEGF antibody, one analyst calls the asset “the next major backbone” of cancer treatment.

title: Plug-and-play gene therapy: FDA executes on vision that’s been in the works for years
snippet: Former biologics boss Peter Marks had a vision. With the FDA’s latest draft guidance, it’s coming to fruition. Speaking with BioSpace, current CBER leader Karim Mikhail said the “adapted pathway” is designed to develop personalized gene therapies more quickly.

title: Can Saudi Arabia's burgeoning biotech hub withstand geopolitical pressures?

title: BridgeBio gears up for rare muscular dystrophy launch with FDA approval in sight
snippet: If approved, BridgeBio Pharma’s BBP-418—which, according to one Jefferies analyst, boasts “pretty darn compelling” data—would be the first therapy for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The FDA has an action date of Nov. 27.

title: AbbVie’s Q3 beat should keep ‘train rolling’ as company eyes bolt-on deals
snippet: Strong immunology and neuroscience sales fueled AbbVie’s latest quarterly beat as the pharma’s stock continues to hit all-time highs.

title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago.
